stopifnot(isTRUE(status$complete), status$completed_method_runs == 180)

runs <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "runs.csv"))

## Question

Can MPCurve recover the number of latent sample orderings when every feature
trajectory is monotone and the true number is three, four, or five? We test
the automatic-$M$ adaptive empirical-Bayes (EB) procedure in **MPCurver
0.3.4** on 90 fixed datasets and compare it with the original adaptive and
uniform-prior forward fits on those same inputs.

## Simulation design

Each dataset has **300 samples and 60 features**. Features belong to equally
sized groups following **3, 4, or 5 independent orderings**, giving 20, 15,
or 12 features per ordering. For sample $i$ and feature $j$,

$$X_{ij}=f_j(t_{i,z_j})+\epsilon_{ij},$$

where $z_j$ identifies the generating ordering, latent positions are
independent Uniform$(0,1)$ draws, and $f_j$ is a smooth monotone curve.
Each curve is a random weighted combination of monotone basis functions,
with its direction chosen to be increasing or decreasing. Under the parameters
used here, most resulting trajectories have mild curvature and are close to
linear. Each noiseless feature is
centered and scaled to sample variance one before independent Gaussian
noise is added.

The variance signal-to-noise ratio is **1, 4, or 16**, corresponding to
noise standard deviations of 1, 0.5, or 0.25. There are **10 independent
datasets for each of the nine conditions**, or **90 datasets in total**.
Separate pilot datasets were used to check the implementation and runtime;
they are excluded from these results.

### Simulated trajectories and observations

Figures 1–3 show **replicate 1 from every condition**. Each row is a
true ordering and each column is an SNR setting. For the first three features
in each group, solid lines show the noiseless signal and points show all 300
noisy observations, plotted against that group's true latent positions.
All panels use the same axis scales. Conditions use independent datasets,
so both the generating curves and noise realizations differ across columns.

```{r estimate-m-design-three, fig.alt="True M equals 3: three ordering rows and three SNR columns, showing noiseless trajectories and noisy observations.", fig.cap="Figure 1. ## Methods

### Automatic-M adaptive EB in MPCurver 0.3.4

The current fit calls `fit_mpcurve(intrinsic_dim = "auto")`. For each feature
pair, it sorts one feature and regresses the other on its rank using a natural
cubic spline with five fixed degrees of freedom. The symmetric similarity is
the larger directional proportion of variance explained. Single-linkage
clustering considers cuts up to eight groups, rejects any cut containing fewer
than two features, and selects the eligible cut with the largest mean
silhouette width.

If the selected group sizes are $d_1,\ldots,d_M$, every feature starts with
the same adaptive ordering probabilities $p(z_j=m)=d_m/60$. Isomap is then
applied independently within each selected feature group. Subsequent EB
updates may remove an occupied ordering, so the reported **effective M** is
the number of slots whose mean posterior assignment probability exceeds
$10^{-12}$.

The current fits use the frozen MPCurver 0.3.4 source at commit
`15f2b0bbe5dfa61cd46da5160b2bc251e75a0475`. They use 50 grid positions,
coordinate-ascent variational inference (CAVI), second-order random-walk
smoothing with `ridge = 0`, adaptive cell-position
priors, estimated feature-specific noise and smoothness, annealing from
temperature five to one, and normalized convergence tolerance $10^{-6}$.

### Original paired controls

The original MPCurver 0.3.2 fits remain paired controls on the same fixed
datasets.

- **Adaptive EB (M = 8):** starts with eight ordering slots and estimates the
  ordering-assignment prior weights.
- **Uniform + forward:** fixes the ordering prior to $1/M$, starts at $M=1$,
  and fits successively larger models up to eight, stopping at the first
  converged candidate whose temperature-one objective does not improve.

These controls used absolute Spearman similarity, single linkage, and Isomap
initialization. All procedures use the same effective-$M$ threshold and a
declared maximum of 10,000 sweeps.

## Recovery of M

Exact recovery, underestimation, overestimation, and unresolved outcomes use
all 10 planned repeats as their denominator. Error bars are 95% Wilson
intervals. The methods are assessed against the generating truth; their
ELBO values are not compared against each other.

The spline-similarity cut selects the true $M$ in
**`r auto_comparison$similarity_cut_exact` of 90 datasets**. After adaptive
EB, automatic-$M$ recovers the true effective $M$ in
**`r auto_adaptive$exact` of 90 datasets**, compared with
**`r old_adaptive$exact`** for the original eight-slot adaptive fit and
**`r old_forward$exact`** for uniform + forward (Figures 4–6 and Table 1).

```{r estimate-m-recovery, fig.cap="Figure 4. Exact effective-M recovery on the all-monotone datasets. Columns show true M; points summarize 10 datasets at each SNR and error bars are 95% Wilson intervals. Automatic-M uses spline variance explained, single linkage, minimum cluster size two, and adaptive EB."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(auto_result_dir, "exact_recovery_comparison.png")))
```

```{r estimate-m-table}

table$method <- unname(current_method_labels[table$method])
names(table) <- c("Method", "Exact M", "Under", "Over", "Mean ARI",
  "Mean ordering score", "Median seconds", "Warnings")

```

## Recovery of the underlying structure

Feature-group recovery is measured by the adjusted Rand index (ARI), assigning
each feature to the ordering with the largest posterior assignment probability.
An ordering with no assigned features does not change this partition.

For ordering recovery, inferred positions are matched one-to-one to the
true orderings by absolute Spearman correlation, allowing reversal of an
axis. Unmatched true orderings contribute zero to the mean recovery score.
These structural summaries describe completed fits; unresolved rates are
reported separately above.

Automatic-$M$ adaptive EB has mean feature-partition ARI
**`r sprintf("%.3f", auto_adaptive$mean_ARI)`** and mean ordering score
**`r sprintf("%.3f", auto_adaptive$mean_ordering_recovery)`**. The corresponding
values are **`r sprintf("%.3f", old_adaptive$mean_ARI)`** and
**`r sprintf("%.3f", old_adaptive$mean_ordering_recovery)`** for the original
adaptive fit, and **`r sprintf("%.3f", old_forward$mean_ARI)`** and
**`r sprintf("%.3f", old_forward$mean_ordering_recovery)`** for uniform +
forward (Figure 7).

```{r estimate-m-structure, fig.cap="Figure 7. Mean feature-partition ARI and ordering recovery for all three procedures. Columns identify true M, rows identify the metric, and points average 10 fixed datasets at each SNR."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(auto_result_dir, "structural_recovery_comparison.png")))
```

## Runtime and convergence

Runtime (Figure 11) includes initialization and every candidate and continuation used
by each method. A forward search therefore includes its rejected stopping
candidate. All workers use one CPU thread.

```{r estimate-m-runtime, fig.cap="Figure 11. Median single-thread fitting time for each procedure, true M, and SNR. Automatic-M includes its similarity calculation and all continuations; forward selection includes every candidate and its stopping candidate."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(auto_result_dir, "runtime_comparison.png")))
```

All **270 method runs** across the current procedure and two paired controls
converged without fitting warnings. Automatic-$M$ adaptive EB has median
runtime **`r sprintf("%.1f", auto_adaptive$median_seconds)` seconds**, compared
with **`r sprintf("%.1f", old_adaptive$median_seconds)` seconds** for the
original adaptive fit and **`r sprintf("%.1f", old_forward$median_seconds)`
seconds** for uniform + forward.

## Summary and reproduction

In this simpler all-monotone setting, the spline-based similarity cut is exact
in **`r auto_comparison$similarity_cut_exact`/90** datasets. Automatic-$M$
adaptive EB finishes with the correct effective count in
**`r auto_adaptive$exact`/90**, compared with **`r old_adaptive$exact`/90** for
the original adaptive fit and **`r old_forward$exact`/90** for uniform +
forward. This benchmark has balanced groups, no garbage features, and a
monotone trajectory for every feature; the one-anchor study tests the harder
trajectory-shape setting.

The [experiment directory](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/InferOrder/tree/master/experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_v032)
contains the fixed design and seeds, scripts, summaries, and standalone
report source. The `auto_m_v034/` extension freezes MPCurver 0.3.4 at commit
`15f2b0bbe5dfa61cd46da5160b2bc251e75a0475`, records the package archive
checksum and input hashes, and fits the same 90 inputs used by the two original
controls.
